literal_meaning: সাপও মরে, লাঠিও না ভাঙে (the snake also dies, the stick also does not break)
figurative_meaning_bn: বিনাক্ষতিতে কঠিন কার্যসিদ্ধি; দুইদিক বজায় থাকা বা রাখা; বিপদ এড়িয়ে কার্যসিদ্ধি করা
figurative_meaning_en: Achieving difficult tasks without harm or loss; maintaining balance on both sides; succeeding while avoiding danger
similar_in_english: Have your cake and eat it too
Kill two birds with one stone
example_sentences_in_bangla: তার চতুরতায় সাপও মরল লাঠিও না ভাঙল।
কূটনীতিতে সাপও মরে লাঠিও না ভাঙে এমনভাবে চুক্তি হল।
example_sentences_in_english: His cleverness ensured the snake died without breaking the stick.
The negotiation achieved success where the snake died but the stick remained unbroken.
history: This idiom draws from rural Bengali folklore, symbolizing efficient action in pest control without wasting resources, common in agrarian society.
note: The idiom emphasizes resourcefulness in traditional village settings.
